EU public procurement notice (TED, published 2026-07-07)
Title: Technology Development Programme Call 2025
Description: The Technology Development Programme (TDP) is a pre-commercial procurement (PCP). PCP challenges innovative players on the market, via an open, transparent and competitive process, to develop new solutions for a technologically demanding mid- to long-term challenge that is in the public interest and requires new Research and Developments (R&D) services, as there are typically no solutions on or close to the market yet. PCP consists in competitive development in stages to identify the solutions offering the best value for money. R&D contracts are awarded to several competing contractors at the same time to compare different approaches to solving the challenge, with the number of competing contractors being reduced after each stage. The TDP Call 2025 consists of six Actions. Each TDP Action will be implemented by means of direct contracts comprising three stages.

Title: C3S2_413_bis Maintenance and Extension of C3S Windstorm and Storm Surge Services
Description: ECMWF, as the Entrusted Entity for the Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S), invites Tenders for the maintenance and extension of C3S windstorm and storm surge services. The requirements are split into two Lots: maintenance and extension of the Operational Windstorm Service (Lot 1), and maintenance and extension of operational storm surge products (Lot 2). Title: Purchase of Soil System
Description: DTU intends to purchase a system for automated long-term observation of greenhouse gases, a Soil Gas Flux System from LI-COR Biosciences GmbH. The highly accurate sensors measure dry mole fractions of CO2 and CH4 with stable sensitivity and negligible noise and consider thus the effect of water vapor dilution from soil evaporation on the measurement. The limited size of the chambers and the multi-gas analytics allow us to employ apparatus over a range of applications above porous GHG emitting media, such es natural soils agricultural soils, landfills and novel biofilters. The system includes eight automated chambers that only close during measurement, keeping chamber effects on the soil minimal. According to the ICOS protocol, we need 16 chamber bases for alternating measurement. 16 Soil sensors will continuously monitor volumetric soil water content and soil temperature.

Title: RFI/Market survey - procurement of level meters for waste containers and containers.
Description: Oslo municipality, c/o the Agency for Waste and Recycling, hereafter called REG, invites tenderers to a market survey (RFI) in connection with the purchase of level meters in waste containers and containers. Data from level meters shall be used for needs based emptying and route optimisation. Another relevant area of use for level meters or equivalent container mounted sensors is to be able to register the position and emptying as an alternative to RFID and vehicle mounted reading equipment. Description: In future, DCC expects to focus increasingly on private supplies, and the applicable legislation requires the same range of tests as at present. Many of these tests are currently outsourced by DCC, meanwhile limits and enforcement are expected to tighten over time. The main focus of the current procurement specification is to bring analyses back in-house and onto DCC’s INAB ISO17025 scope, to maximise 1. DCC’s ability to implement its current and future statutory testing 3. DCC testing capability to serve Local Authorities around Ireland 4. Provision of impartial means for DCC to verify the effectiveness of water management initiatives for Climate and Urban Resilience. Title: Market consultation portal & viewer of the Dutch Satellite Data Portal

Title: A universal testing machine for tensile and compressive load tests, equipped with two additional actuators (1 unit)
Description: The Department of Steel and Composite Structures at ETH Zurich is planning to procure a new universal testing machine for the construction hall at the Hönggerberg site. The equipment is intended to test large-scale components under realistic static and dynamic loads, thereby supporting future research in steel, composite and earthquake engineering. The machine must provide a spacious test chamber capable of accommodating test specimens up to “B: 1500 mm, H: 1500 mm, L: 5000 mm”. Description: The objective of the procurement is to replace six existing passenger lifts/bed lifts from 1978. The lifts are located in the Central Block by Førde Central Hospital. The lifts have a payload of 1,200 kg per lift and are used by employees, patients and visitors at the hospital. All lifts have nine stops with through doors except level 0, 1 and 2 with fewer number of doors. The current lifts shall be demolished and new lifts that shall be assembled in the existing shafts shall be installed.
